papers.title: Close notice
lines: The close is to be washed on Tuesdays by the top floor, Wednesdays by the middle floor, Thursdays by the ground floor.
Friday is for arguing about it.

papers.title: Up Helly Aa squad list
lines: Jarl's squad: forty-one men, all in horned helmets, all in good spirits, mostly in good order.
The galley will be burned at dusk. The after-party will be burned at dawn.

papers.title: Scorecard
lines: Old Course, the Road Hole. Score: nine. Excuses: seven.
Caddie's comment: 'I am sure you have other talents, sir.'

papers.title: Distiller's note
lines: The angels' share took another two per cent this year. We are not pleased.
We have told the angels. They have not replied.

trail.clue: A distiller buried a hip flask near the big rock to leave for a rainy day.

papers.title: Tram conductor's note
lines: Last tram on the line tonight. People are crying, which is silly. It was only a tram.
I punched a few extra tickets as keepsakes. Nobody will mind. The company is not what it was.

papers.title: Ferry ticket
lines: Mallaig to Armadale, return. Bring a coat. The ferry will say it is not rough. The ferry is a liar.
On the back: 'Sea-sick. Worth it.'

trail.clue: A fellow traveller buried a flask of tea near the old oak, 'for the next soaked soul'.

papers.title: Fringe flyer
lines: Come and see a one-man show about a one-man show about a man who was once in a show.
Tickets: seven pounds. Refunds: not a concept.

papers.title: Boatman's log
lines: Tuesday: saw a log. Wednesday: saw a different log. Thursday: saw a visitor who thought the log was a monster.
I did not correct him. He tipped well.

trail.clue: A boatman's tip jar lies buried near the old oak, 'where the monster won't look'.

papers.title: Mason's tally
lines: Forty blocks of granite for the new bank. Each weighs as much as a small cow.
The mason would like it noted that he has been doing this since the Boer War and nobody has yet said thank you.

papers.title: Letter from the croft
lines: Dear Calum, the potatoes are in and the weather is not. The cow has a cold.
Come home when the herring come. The ceilidh will be on, and your mother has been baking.

papers.title: Ferry crossing slip
lines: Oban to Mull, one car, one van, forty-two sheep, two dogs and a man with a harp.
The harp has right of way. The sheep have strong opinions.

papers.title: Weaver's order
lines: Orb stamped, three hundred yards of tweed for the London shop. Must be woven in the weaver's own home, as the law says.
The weaver sings Gaelic waulking songs while treadling. The customers are never told.

trail.clue: A weaver's spare shuttle and some coin lie near the big rock. 'For the day the loom is silent.'

papers.title: Dundee mill note
lines: Jute, jam and journalism: that is what we make here, and we do all three badly on Mondays.
The marmalade is a point of civic pride. The jute is a point of civic regret.

papers.title: Ceilidh card
lines: Strip the Willow, Dashing White Sergeant, Gay Gordons, Eightsome Reel, and a slow waltz at the end.
If you are not out of breath, you have not been trying.

papers.title: Mountain rescue card
lines: If lost: stay still, stay warm, blow three blasts on your whistle, and wait for a man with a flask.
If found by the wrong man, apologise anyway.

papers.title: Handwritten tale
lines: There was a fisherman who took a sealskin from a rock. He kept a wife for seven years.
In the eighth she found the skin. The tale says she went home. The tale does not say what she told the neighbours.
